papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: The authors adapted a weight-drop mouse model of traumatic brain injury to allow EEG/EMG recording and found that mild TBI produces cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and diffuse axonal injury. Treatment with sodium oxybate during the first three days after trauma increased slow-wave activity and reduced axonal injury, whereas chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons did not reduce slow-wave activity.

papers.title: Comparison and extension of the Riemannian Procrustes analysis and tangent space alignment transfer learning methods.
papers.summary: Compares Riemannian Procrustes analysis (RPA) and tangent space alignment (TSA) for transfer learning on motor-imagery EEG across six public datasets, and tests analytic versus standard Hermitian/symmetric positive definite covariance representations. With substantial target-domain knowledge TSA outperformed RPA and analytic covariance matrices outperformed standard ones, while with limited target data performance depended on available target data and source-data selection mattered.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Proxies of Cortical Excitability in Epilepsy: Group Discrimination, Temporal Stability and Medication Sensitivity
papers.summary: Analyzing 1,404 scalp EEG recordings from 96 epilepsy patients and 85 healthy controls, this study evaluated eight EEG-derived markers of cortical excitability and found that only aperiodic offset and exponent showed FDR-robust group differences, with aperiodic offset higher in epilepsy. Both aperiodic measures were more reproducible across sessions in epilepsy, and higher antiseizure medication burden was associated with higher relative alpha power.

papers.title: iEEG Can Help EEG: Improving Clinical Scalp EEG Analysis through Intracranial Priors
papers.summary: Proposes ReBrain, a cross-modal framework that fits a signal-to-signal model on intracranial EEG alone, freezes it as a prior, and re-expresses scalp EEG through it without paired data or fine-tuning. ReBrain consistently improved host downstream models across recordings from multiple hospitals and architecture families, with analysis attributing gains to neural structure carried by iEEG.

papers.title: Frequency-Specific Thalamocortical Network Dynamics During Focal Seizures in Humans.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed simultaneous cortical and thalamic stereoelectroencephalography in 19 pediatric-onset drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients (66 seizures), using spectral power, imaginary coherence, and spectral Granger causality across slow, beta, and gamma bands. Found frequency-specific bidirectional thalamocortical interactions with large slow-band thalamus-to-seizure-onset-zone outflow near termination, and thalamic EEG features classified seizure state with AUC 0.825 (AN) and 0.839 (CM).

papers.title: Best1 shapes the depth and stability of NREM sleep.
papers.summary: Used immunohistochemistry and EEG/EMG polysomnography in Best1 knockout mice to test whether the astrocytic calcium-activated anion channel Best1 regulates sleep architecture. Best1-KO mice showed selective disruption of deep NREM sleep with shorter deep NREM bouts, attenuated delta-band (0.5-4 Hz) power, and reduced entry into and maintenance of deep NREM despite preserved total sleep time.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Ecological and integrative physiology
papers.summary: Monitored locomotor activity in CD-1 mice, Mongolian gerbils, and white-tailed antelope squirrels and applied Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to quantify circadian and infradian rhythms. Circadian rhythms were robust in all animals, whereas infradian (5- and 10-day) rhythmicity was extremely low in mice and moderate in gerbils and squirrels, with strength under 10% of circadian rhythmicity.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.summary: Using identical frozen ATCNet/FBCNet representations compared across BCI2a, OpenBMI, BCI2b, and BNCI2015-001, this work demonstrates a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect in which CLIF-family temporal-state decoders outperform ANN-SEW by 10.082 pp (BCI2a) and 5.470 pp (OpenBMI) under cross-entropy-only training, with attenuation as labels increase (-2.319 pp per label doubling in BNCI2015-001). Hard binary spikes were not necessary, and matched whole-sequence readout reduced CLIF-versus-continuous-decoder differences.

papers.title: Image-grounded encoding models reveal distinct temporal profiles of naturalistic object and scene processing in the human brain
papers.summary: Using image-grounded deep neural network encoding models to predict human EEG responses to natural images, this study found that models trained on object-bound features consistently showed a delayed temporal encoding profile compared with models trained on scene-bound features. The distinct encoding profiles were used to reveal the typicality of individual image elements as objects or scene parts, indicating differential temporal unfolding of object and scene processing.

papers.title: Investigating Modified Deep Learning Models for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Classification Using Electroencephalography Spectrograms.
papers.summary: Band-shuffle augmentation, a neurophysiologically informed strategy that exchanges spectral content within canonical EEG frequency bands between same-class samples, improved EEG-spectrogram deep learning classification of pediatric ADHD, yielding 75.05% accuracy and 75.76% F1 versus 74.32% for traditional image augmentation. An adaptive multistrategy pipeline reached 77.47% accuracy and 0.8414 AUC, 27.0% above the MobileNetV2 baseline and 4.2% above conventional augmentation, with Grad-CAM highlighting ADHD-consistent frequency regions.

papers.title: Motor Imagery Classification Using Hybrid Cross-Subject Class Mixup and Selective Attention
papers.summary: The authors propose a hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor-imagery decoding framework combining Cross-Subject Class Mixup, which mixes modality-specific donor trials from other subjects within the anchor class, with a Selective Attention architecture retaining causal temporal self-attention for EEG and a CLS token for multimodal fusion. In leave-one-subject-out evaluation across 28 subjects on a public dataset, it achieved 76.85% mean balanced accuracy and 76.58% macro-F1, the highest among five reimplemented baselines.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-derived spectral edge frequency 95 targets in toddlers under propofol anaesthesia✰.
papers.summary: In 51 toddlers aged 13–24 months undergoing propofol anaesthesia, the prospective study used Dixon up-and-down and isotonic regression to establish SEF95 targets for pacifier placement (ED50 21.8 Hz; ED90 20.3 Hz), electrical nerve stimulation (12.0; 10.4 Hz), and laryngoscopy (10.3; 4.4 Hz). SEF95 was inversely related to plasma propofol (0.21 μg ml-1 decrease per Hz; r=0.46, P<0.001), supporting age-specific EEG-guided propofol titration.

papers.title: Signatures of Performance Monitoring in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and At-risk Groups: Midfrontal Theta Predicts Divergent Behavioral Adaptation.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
papers.summary: In 180 adults (OCD, unaffected first-degree relatives, adverse childhood experiences, controls) performing a flanker task, error-related midfrontal theta was enhanced in OCD but not in at-risk groups. Trial-wise coupling was altered: greater theta predicted slower, less accurate subsequent trials in OCD versus improved performance in controls, paralleling prolonged post-error slowing in OCD and linking theta to worry and depressive symptoms.

papers.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals.
papers.summary: Presents MyoGen, an open-source framework unifying spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Benchmarking against human motor unit recordings showed simulated population activity matched experimental discharge-rate distributions and reproduced beta-band modulation of descending drive and low-dimensional agonist-antagonist EMG control manifolds.

papers.title: Knockdown of KCNQ2 in CA1 reshapes epilepsy-related limbic network rhythms and reduces spontaneous exploratory behavior in mice.
papers.summary: Knocked down KCNQ2 in mouse hippocampal CA1 via AAV-shRNA and recorded cell-type-specific calcium activity with multi-site EEG to characterize limbic network changes during epileptogenesis. CA1 KCNQ2 loss disrupted excitatory/inhibitory balance and produced biphasic network changes, with reduced low-frequency power and connectivity followed by hypersynchronization during severe seizures, plus altered phase-amplitude coupling and exploratory/social behavioral deficits partially rescued by retigabine.

papers.title: From Variability to Synchrony: Non-linear Development of Auditory Neural Responses During the First Year of Life.
papers.summary: Followed 69 infants with high-density EEG at 2 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months to track auditory evoked responses to pure tones. Auditory responses became more pronounced with reduced trial-to-trial variability, and low-frequency inter-trial phase coherence rose from 2 weeks to later stages but decreased from 6 to 12 months, indicating a non-linear synchronization trajectory.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.summary: Developed an immersive virtual reality replica of a prior real multisensory environment intervention and assessed EEG spectral and nonlinear features before and after exposure in 31 healthy participants, with the real-MSE data used only as a qualitative reference. The alpha/beta ratio (negatively correlated with stress) was the only feature significantly increased in both conditions, while in the V-MSE frontal theta and theta/beta ratio rose and relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity fell.

papers.title: Neural Tracking of Continuous Speech Is Sensitive to Socially "Engaging" Prosodic Features of Conversational Anecdotes.
papers.summary: Used EEG-based neural speech tracking in 31 listeners hearing gossip-like anecdotes varying in topic interest and engaging versus neutral prosody, with time-bidding as a behavioral engagement measure. Engaging prosody enhanced frontal neural speech tracking only for interesting topics, and alpha power showed a distinct interaction at left-anterior sites, indicating prosodic effects on speech encoding depend on contextual motivation.

papers.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
papers.summary: Recorded EEG during four attentional control paradigms (change detection, go/no-go, Simon, Stroop) and tested whether P3 and decoding-accuracy measures load onto a common latent attentional-control factor. Despite robust within-task group-level effects, correlations were weak and structural equation modeling found no evidence for a common latent factor, questioning the construct validity of these EEG indices for individual differences.

papers.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans.
papers.summary: In 68 stroke patients performing a trial-and-error guessing task, voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping showed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c' and 32' significantly attenuated the reward positivity (RewP) ERP amplitude, supporting a single caudal anterior cingulate generator underlying goal-completion signaling.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 26,168 pediatric anesthetic records found that routine intraoperative raw EEG use rose from 17.8% to 28.4% of cases between October 2024 and June 2026, with wide provider-level variation (median 18.1%, range 0.9%-79.5%) only weakly explained by case mix.

papers.title: Toward Closed-Loop Cognitive Modulation in Alzheimer's Disease: BCI-Relevant Evidence and a Translational Roadmap.
papers.summary: This narrative review maps BCI and closed-loop evidence in Alzheimer's disease and MCI across read (EEG, fNIRS, real-time fMRI, fUS, t-ULM), control, and write (neurofeedback, tACS, tDCS, rTMS, TUS, FUS-BBB opening) modules, proposing a translational roadmap centered on adaptive-versus-fixed delivery trials with prespecified decoding, safety, and target-engagement endpoints.

papers.title: Impaired cortical gap-mediated inhibition in chronic tinnitus but with limited individual diagnostic accuracy
papers.summary: In a prospective multicentre case-control EEG study (232 chronic tinnitus cases, 223 controls), tinnitus was associated with reduced broadband gap-mediated inhibition of the N100 response (beta=-19.27%, d=-0.413, p=0.002) scaling with severity, but individual discrimination was limited (AUC 0.612), indicating a group-level rather than diagnostic marker.

papers.title: Differential associations of contralesional and ipsilesional brain functional connectivity with lower-limb impairment after stroke.
papers.summary: In 18 chronic stroke survivors, resting-state EEG showed that contralesional hemisphere functional connectivity was associated with greater hip flexion ROM interlimb asymmetry (r=0.53; 28% of variance) and contralesional M1 connectivity with slower 10-m walk time (r=0.51; 26% of variance), while ipsilesional connectivity showed no significant relationships.

papers.title: Microstate-specific functional connectivity in alcohol use disorder using resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: Using resting-state EEG microstate analysis in 26 young adults with alcohol use disorder (AUD) and 35 healthy controls, this study found AUD temporal dynamics biased toward microstates C and D, with greater frontal-occipital but reduced interhemispheric functional connectivity within microstate C. Microstate-specific connectivity classified groups better than conventional connectivity and revealed less stable hub-like properties in AUD, suggesting it as an informative neural marker.

papers.title: Invasive monitoring and mapping in epilepsy surgery: Acute and chronic intracranial recording from surface to depth.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
authors: Tatiana V H F de Oliveira
papers.summary: An ILAE Surgical Therapies Commission education review of invasive intracranial monitoring and mapping for drug-resistant focal epilepsy, covering the historical shift from intraoperative electrocorticography and subdural recording to stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG). It compares subdural and stereotactic approaches on coverage, mapping capability, diagnostic yield, seizure outcome, and morbidity, emphasizing that electrode choice should follow a stated anatomo-electro-clinical hypothesis.

papers.title: Distinct cortical functional network alterations in internet gaming disorder and alcohol use disorder: A resting-state EEG graph theory analysis.
papers.summary: This study applied resting-state EEG source reconstruction and graph theory to compare cortical networks in 49 patients with internet gaming disorder (IGD), 48 with alcohol use disorder (AUD), and 54 healthy controls. IGD showed significantly higher beta-band clustering coefficient and strength, especially in parietal and limbic regions, while bilateral superior frontal nodal beta measures were lower in AUD than IGD, indicating distinct cortical network patterns between the addictions.

papers.title: A novel theta-frequency tACS approach for major depressive disorder: Initial findings from an open-label pilot study.
papers.summary: This open-label pilot study tested 20 sessions of individualized theta-frequency tACS over bilateral prefrontal cortex during working memory tasks in 11 adults with moderate-to-severe major depressive disorder. Treatment was feasible and well tolerated, with MADRS scores decreasing significantly and endpoint response/remission rates of 80%/60% (80%/70% at follow-up); greater individualized theta power increases were associated with greater symptom reductions, though the open-label design limits interpretation.

papers.title: Electrophysiological dynamics of empathy for self- and other-related pain
papers.summary: In 42 female participants viewing self- and other-related painful versus neutral facial expressions, this EEG study found an early self-other distinction, with self-related painful stimuli eliciting more negative N2 amplitudes and greater alpha/mu suppression than other-related painful stimuli. In the late stage this distinction disappeared, with painful expressions regardless of self/other producing larger late positive potentials, suggesting early self-other separation followed by later convergence in empathic processing.

papers.title: Longitudinal exploration of auditory sensory-perceptual processing in CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (Batten disease)): A high-density auditory evoked potential (AEP) study.
papers.summary: This exploratory longitudinal case series used high-density EEG with a duration mismatch negativity paradigm to track auditory evoked potentials in 4 individuals with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease versus 60 neurotypical controls. N1 and P2 amplitude differences were most pronounced at the slowest presentation rate, shifting from more negative to more positive amplitudes with age, and more positive N1 during the longest stimulus condition was associated with reduced verbal intelligence and working memory, supporting auditory EEG as an objective translational outcome measure.

papers.title: Sensitivity of ECG QRS complexes to His-Purkinje structure in whole-heart electrophysiology models.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: Generated 22,528 rule-based fractal-tree His-Purkinje system (HPS) models with varied structural parameters and used Sobol sensitivity analysis to assess effects on simulated QRS metrics in a whole-heart monodomain electrophysiology model. Most moderate HPS structural perturbations produced limited changes in diagnostically relevant QRS features, though rare (<1%) aberrant networks caused abnormal QRS morphology, suggesting generic HPS geometry suffices for normal sinus-rhythm simulations.

papers.title: Automated extraction of seizures and ictal-interictal continuum patterns from EEG reports to enable large-scale neurophysiology and neurocritical care research.
papers.summary: Developed and validated a five-stage hybrid rule-based plus large language model pipeline to extract seizures, periodic/rhythmic patterns, and ictal-interictal continuum features from free-text EEG reports across 156,582 reports from three health systems. Average seizure detection accuracy was 0.94, with pattern detection accuracies of 0.96-0.97 for LPD, GPD, and GRDA/LRDA, enabling scalable neurophysiology and neurocritical care research.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 216 pediatric video-EEG report episodes, a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge burden abstracted from qualitative report wording was associated with new antiseizure medication initiation within 7 days (adjusted OR 2.89 per higher burden grade; initiation rates 13.0%, 42.9%, 70.0%). Treatment intensification findings in the established-epilepsy cohort were exploratory and non-causal.

papers.title: Neurophysiological and Sleep-Related Effects of a Cosmetic Shampoo and Conditioner Regimen in Adults with Scalp Discomfort: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: Single-arm observational pilot in 21 adults with scalp discomfort and mild sleep disturbance tested a cosmetic shampoo/conditioner regimen for 2 weeks, finding significant improvements in EEG mood valence and sleepiness, all four sleep questionnaires, scalp itch intensity (49.1% reduction), and weekly discomfort days (40.6% reduction). An exploratory subgroup showed increased deep sleep on wearable tracking, described as hypothesis-generating only.

papers.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy: A retrospective observational study at a tertiary care hospital.
papers.summary: Retrospective observational study of 382 patients with epilepsy at a tertiary hospital in Karachi found a 19.4% prevalence of drug-resistant epilepsy. Normal MRI (aOR 0.29) and normal EEG (aOR 0.50) were associated with lower odds of resistance, while lower education (aOR 3.50) and history of status epilepticus (aOR 8.03) were associated with higher odds.

papers.title: Mismatched findings on ancillary examinations in virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis: pathological mechanisms and clinical significance.
papers.summary: This review proposes a conceptual framework grouping viral encephalitis, post-infectious autoimmune encephalitis, and acute encephalopathy syndromes without direct CNS infection under the term virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis, categorized by distinct pathogenic mechanisms. It analyzes common causes of mismatched ancillary findings (neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid, electroencephalography) across disease stages and mechanisms, and recommends prompt empirical intravenous acyclovir when HSV or VZV encephalitis is clinically suspected.

papers.title: Neurophysiological changes following intensive Naikan therapy in a patient with recurrent depressive episodes later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder: A case report.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
papers.summary: In a 29-year-old man with recurrent depressive episodes later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder, 7 days of intensive Naikan therapy was associated with decreased anxiety and depressive symptoms, reduced resting-state beta-band global field power, and increased P300 amplitude, though sLORETA was descriptive only. The single uncontrolled case is hypothesis-generating and does not establish efficacy or mechanism.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.summary: Using mouse and human data, this study shows a circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node that prolongs PR interval during sleep and is largely independent of vagal tone, driven instead by a local circadian clock; Bmal1 knockout reduced the PR rhythm by ~43-52%. Molecular remodeling includes rhythms in >300 signaling molecules and ~15% of 4,186 proteins, including ion channels, with reduced L-type Ca2+ current and upstroke velocity during sleep confirmed by computer modeling.

papers.title: A Novel DHX9 Variant Was Identified in a Patient With Developmental Delay, Facial Dysmorphism and Seizure.
papers.journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
papers.summary: Reports a female patient with DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder presenting global developmental delay, ASD, facial dysmorphism, epilepsy, microcephaly, and abnormal brain MRI, carrying a likely de novo missense variant p.(His514Tyr) in the conserved DEIH helicase motif; structural modeling suggested altered hydrogen bonding and local stability, expanding the DHX9 variant phenotypic spectrum.

papers.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice.
papers.summary: Using Duplex Sequencing, the authors assessed mutagenicity of a coal tar-based driveway sealant extract in MutaMouse male mice and found significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency in liver and bone marrow, with spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions resembling a tobacco-smoking-associated mutational signature. Germ cells showed no statistically significant increase by duplex sequencing but a positive dose-response trend, with mutagenicity supported by a significant increase in mutant frequency in the lacZ plaque assay.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
